query: Using MuJoCo in Python, solve IK for a top-down grasp (tool axis pointing straight down) at target_pos = [0.85, 0.40, 0.05] m for a 5-DOF SO-101 arm, and move the arm there.
expected_behavior: Evaluates kinematic reachability and solver residual against a tolerance before executing any robot motion
Refuses arm motion and raises an error when the target exceeds the reach envelope (~0.35 m) instead of executing an unconverged position
Formulates 5-DOF IK with 3D position and tool-axis-down alignment constraints
Dispatches actuator commands through ctrl rather than qpos teleporting

query: Turn this into a FastAPI app that runs the simulation in real time and serves both a live rendered camera stream (MJPEG) and the state endpoint. It will run on a headless Linux server.
expected_behavior: Runs physics stepping in exactly one dedicated background thread, keeping route handlers free of mj_step calls
Runs offscreen rendering on a dedicated thread with EGL context affinity instead of calling renderer in request handlers
Serves state from thread-safe cached snapshots or via asyncio.to_thread without blocking the asyncio event loop
Configures headless EGL rendering (MUJOCO_GL=egl) before importing mujoco

query: In a MuJoCo SO-101 simulation (Menagerie robotstudio_so101) the cube slips out of the gripper during the lift. Here is the pick code. Fix it so the grasp holds.
expected_behavior: Drives arm and gripper actuators via data.ctrl rather than teleporting joint positions with data.qpos
Adds friction pads to gripper jaws with collision bitmasks (contype/conaffinity) so pads collide with objects but not with each other or the floor
Limits gripper actuator force within a stable gripping window (~1.5 N·m) to prevent ejecting the cube
Pauses for servo convergence (settling position error and velocity) before executing the lift
